subject.title: fix(message): ignore populated Telegram location on model sends

question: Should OpenClaw approve `internal.agentRuntimeIdentity.messageActionContext` as the boundary that permits a model-tool-originated Telegram send to discard a populated location while direct/API mixed sends continue to fail closed?
rationale: Source evidence supports that ordinary direct/API clients cannot mint this local signed identity, but silently changing delivery for that privileged origin is an intentional trust-and-product boundary rather than a mechanical test decision.

options.title: Approve the private origin boundary
options.body: After rebasing and green exact-head CI, accept the scoped model-tool repair while retaining strict rejection for all direct/API requests.

options.title: Keep all populated mixed requests strict
options.body: Pause or close this PR and require a different model-tool/schema strategy that never discards a populated location.

recommendation.title: Approve the private origin boundary
recommendation.body: After rebasing and green exact-head CI, accept the scoped model-tool repair while retaining strict rejection for all direct/API requests.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent current-main location-validation repair whose strict public behavior this PR preserves.
